## What it is

AnythingLLM lets you chat with your own documents: you upload files or links into workspaces, and a language model answers with citations from them. It also runs agents with tools ([Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm](https://github.com/Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm)).

**Licence:** `MIT` (GitHub licence API; license-matrix row "AnythingLLM"). Market class **L1**.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): ai: chat, rag, agents. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`), one container (server and document collector), as the image's own `anythingllm` user (UID 1000). No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- Upstream's compose file adds the `SYS_ADMIN` capability (used by the Chromium sandbox when it scrapes web pages). This package adds no capabilities. **UNVERIFIED:** whether link scraping works without it; uploading files does not need it.
- Volume: `anything-llm-data` (20 GiB): database, documents, vector store and the `.env` file where AnythingLLM saves the settings you choose in its UI. An init container creates that file and adds a random `JWT_SECRET` once (sign-in tokens need it).
- `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true`: no anonymous usage data is sent.
- **x86 CPUs need AVX2** ([system requirements](https://github.com/Mintplex-Labs/anythingllm-docs/blob/main/pages/installation-docker/system-requirements.mdx)): the built-in LanceDB vector store stops the server with "Illegal instruction" on older CPUs or virtual CPUs that hide AVX2. The Market's placement facets cannot express a CPU feature yet.
- Probes: `GET /api/ping` (upstream's health check script).

## First run

Source: [docs.anythingllm.com](https://docs.anythingllm.com) (Docker quickstart).

1. Install AnythingLLM from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-anything-llm`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:3001:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-anything-llm port-forward svc/anything-llm 3001:3001
   ```
3. The onboarding asks for a language model. For a local model, install Ollama from the Market and enter its in-cluster address, `http://ollama.app-ollama.svc:11434` (cross-namespace traffic is allowed until per-app network policies exist).
4. Choose single-user mode with a password, or multi-user mode with an admin account. Do this right after install: until then anyone who can reach the page can use it.

## Not done yet

- Link scraping without `SYS_ADMIN` is untested (above).
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: the entrypoint runs `prisma generate`, which writes into the image.
- Resource figures follow upstream's minimum (2 GB, 2 cores); they are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212771377, job `gate (anything-llm)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/mintplexlabs/anythingllm:1.19.0`: CRITICAL with a fix: `linux-libc-dev` 6.8.0-147.147 (fixed 6.8.0-149.149; for example CVE-2026-89708, CVE-2026-90037, CVE-2026-98365, CVE-2026-98432, CVE-2026-98621, CVE-2026-98725, CVE-2026-98805); `basic-ftp` 5.0.5 CVE-2026-27699 (fixed 5.2.0); `fast-xml-parser` 4.5.0 CVE-2026-25896 (fixed 4.5.4); `protobufjs` CVE-2026-41242 and CVE-2023-36665; `proxy-addr` 2.0.7 CVE-2026-90711 (fixed 2.0.8); `tar` 6.2.1 CVE-2026-59873 (fixed 7.5.19). The full list is in the CI job log.
- Secret finding (Trivy): `gitlab-pat` (CRITICAL) in `/app/server/public/assets/index-fadede8f.js` (a pattern match inside upstream's built front-end bundle).
- Recorded only (no fix available): `decompress` CVE-2026-101894 and CVE-2026-53486, `expr-eval` CVE-2026-12866, more `linux-libc-dev` CVEs. The app still carries `UNVERIFIED` markers (README).
- Passed: ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 200).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.
